correctness.rationale: Facet areas give the claimed incenter, and direct equidistance gives the circumcenter. The two-dimensional collinearity determinant factors as \((p-h)Q\). Fresh symbolic reconstruction verified the squared identity reducing \(Q=0\) to \((p+h)^2=4ph(ph+2)^2/(5ph+6)\); the discriminant is nonnegative exactly from \(ph\ge2\), while the unsquared left side is then positive, so no extraneous solutions survive. For \(ph=3\), the exact branch has discriminant \(16/7\) and the sign term \(110/7>0\); the displayed \((\sqrt7,3/\sqrt7)\) center relation and nonorthogonality test are exact. The edge-length pattern excludes both biregular partition types.
residual_risks: The classification is only for the normalized two-parameter family, not all reflection-symmetric tetrahedra.

final_claim: For \(T_{p,h}=\operatorname{conv}\{(-1,0,0),(1,0,0),(0,p,0),(0,0,h)\}\), the incenter lies on the Euler affine hull exactly when \(p=h\) or \(ph\ge2\) and \((p+h)^2=4ph(ph+2)^2/(5ph+6)\); the latter branch contains explicit non-orthocentric, non-biregular tetrahedra.
limitations: The classification is only for the normalized two-parameter family, not all reflection-symmetric tetrahedra.
